parameters.description:
If `True`, center the data before scaling.
This will cause :meth:`transform` to raise an exception when attempted
on sparse matrices, because centering them entails building a dense
matrix which in common use cases is likely to be too large to fit in
memory.
parameters.name: with_centering

parameters.description: If `True`, scale the data to interquartile range.
parameters.name: with_scaling

parameters.description:
Quantile range used to calculate `scale_`. By default this is equal to
the IQR, i.e., `q_min` is the first quantile and `q_max` is the third
quantile.

.. versionadded:: 0.18
parameters.name: quantile_range

parameters.description:
If `False`, try to avoid a copy and do inplace scaling instead.
This is not guaranteed to always work inplace; e.g. if the data is
not a NumPy array or scipy.sparse CSR matrix, a copy may still be
returned.
parameters.name: copy

parameters.description:
If `True`, scale data so that normally distributed features have a
variance of 1. In general, if the difference between the x-values of
`q_max` and `q_min` for a standard normal distribution is greater
than 1, the dataset will be scaled down. If less than 1, the dataset
will be scaled up.

.. versionadded:: 0.24
parameters.name: unit_variance

signature: RobustScaler(*, with_centering=True, with_scaling=True, quantile_range=(25.0, 75.0), copy=True, unit_variance=False)
summary: Scale features using statistics that are robust to outliers.
